stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Move the $R$, $L$ and $C$ sliders. The Bode magnitude curve peaks at the resonant frequency $f_0 = 1/(2\pi\sqrt{L\,C})$ and drops off on either side. $R$ controls the sharpness (quality factor $Q$ and bandwidth $\Delta f$). Advance after visiting at least $3$ different $f_0$ decades.
stages.concept: A series R-L-C band-pass filter (output across $R$) has $|H(f)| = 1/\sqrt{1 + Q^2\,(f/f_0 - f_0/f)^2}$ with $f_0 = 1/(2\pi\sqrt{L\,C})$ and $Q = 2\pi\,f_0\,L/R$. At $f_0$ the reactances of $L$ and $C$ cancel, current is maximum and $|H| = 0\,\text{dB}$. The bandwidth between the two $-3\,\text{dB}$ points is $\Delta f = f_0/Q$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Tune $L$ and $C$ so the peak sits on the dashed orange line at $f_0 = 2\,\text{kHz}$. Many $(L, C)$ pairs work — you need $L\,C = 1/(2\pi\,f_0)^2$. $R$ does not change $f_0$; it only widens or narrows the peak.
stages.concept: Design: $L\,C = 1/(2\pi\,f_0)^2$. For $f_0 = 2000\,\text{Hz}$: $L\,C \approx 6.33\times10^{-9}\,\text{s}^2$. Examples: $L = 6.33\,\text{mH}$ with $C = 1\,\mu\text{F}$, or $L = 63.3\,\text{mH}$ with $C = 100\,\text{nF}$. Only the product matters for $f_0$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Component values are hidden. Read the resonant frequency $f_0$ off the Bode magnitude curve — it is the peak (where $|H| = 0\,\text{dB}$). Answer every question correctly in one pass; a wrong answer restarts the deck.
stages.concept: Reading $f_0$: locate the top of the peak, then drop a vertical line to the frequency axis. The two $-3\,\text{dB}$ points on either side bracket the bandwidth $\Delta f$; the peak sits (in log terms) between them.

labels.question: question
labels.evaluate_prompt: Component values hidden. Read f_0 (the peak) from the Bode plot alone.
labels.tip1: L↑ or C↑ → peak shifts left ;  f_0 = 1/(2π·√(L·C))
labels.tip2: adjust L·C until the peak sits on the orange line ;  R only sets width
labels.tip3: read f_0 at the peak — one wrong answer restarts the deck
labels.peek_tip_1: At $f = f_0$ the magnitude is maximum ($0\,\text{dB}$). Find the top of the peak and read the x-axis.
labels.peek_tip_2: The two $-3\,\text{dB}$ crossings straddle $f_0$. On a log axis, $f_0$ sits at the geometric mean: $f_0 = \sqrt{f_L\,f_H}$.
labels.peek_tip_3: The phase curve crosses $0°$ exactly at $f_0$. Trace the phase line down to the axis at the zero-crossing.

1.1: The purple dot marks f_0, the peak of the curve. Try increasing L and watch it slide left.
1.2: f_0 = 1/(2π·√(L·C)). Doubling L drops f_0 by √2. R alone does not move f_0 — it only changes Q.
1.3: Visit 3 decades: try small L·C (peak near 100 kHz), medium (near 1 kHz), and large (near 100 Hz).

2.1: You need L·C = 1/(2π·2000)² ≈ 6.33×10⁻⁹ s². Pick a round C then compute L.
2.2: Try C = 1 µF. Then L = 6.33×10⁻⁹ / 10⁻⁶ = 6.33 mH.
2.3: Or C = 100 nF with L = 63.3 mH. Or C = 10 µF with L = 0.633 mH. R is free — it only sets width.

3.1: Find the top of the peak. That frequency is f_0.
3.2: The −3 dB reference line crosses the curve twice. f_0 is halfway between the crossings on the log axis (geometric mean).
3.3: Cross-check with the phase plot: phase = 0° at f_0. Read the x-axis at the phase zero-crossing.
